title: Cap. IV Arg. 4 Sol: John 6:37 — donation causes coming; elegit in Christo mis-exposed
pass_a_gloss: Hither avail those words of Christ at John 6:37. Whatever the Father gives me will come to me. This donation designates the eternal election of God: To come denotes faith produced in human hearts in its time: from the donation is hinted the antecedent cause of coming, that is, of believing: but not foreseen faith the antecedent cause of giving, that is, of electing. But what they bring for confirmation of the Major, That God cannot elect in Christ him who is not in Christ: But those only are in Christ who are considered by God as inserted into Christ through faith: therefore believers alone are elected: this argumentation rests on a false exposition of those Apostolic words, He chose us in Christ.
pass_b_english: John 6:37 helps here: Whatever the Father gives me will come to me. The donation marks God's eternal election; coming marks faith produced in human hearts in its time. Donation is the antecedent cause of coming (believing) — not foreseen faith the antecedent cause of giving (electing). Their Major confirmation — God cannot elect in Christ one who is not in Christ; only those considered inserted into Christ by faith are in Christ; therefore only believers are elected — rests on a false reading of He chose us in Christ.
source_text: Huc faciunt illa Christi verba apud Johannem vi. 37. Quicquid mihi dat Pater, ad me veniet. Donatio haec aeternam Dei electionem designat: Venire, fidem in humanis cordibus suo tempore productam denotat: a donatio innuitur causa antecedanea veniendi, id est, credendi: non autem fides praevisa causa antecedanea donandi, hoc est, eligendi. Quod autem afferunt ad Majoris confirmationem, Deum non posse illum eligere in Christo qui non est in Christo: Illi autem tantum in Christo sunt, qui a Deo considerantur ut Christo inserti per fidem: ergo soli credentes eliguntur: haec argumentatio nititur falsa expositione illorum verborum Apostolicorum, Elegit nos in Christo.
